changes.change:
AC12 now uses the validator’s sweep: `find ~/.claude <общая папка> -name node_modules -prune -o -path '*/.claude/settings*.json' -print | xargs grep -l pixel-office` must print exactly <папка Sai>/.claude/settings.json. It runs in the UAT step and at RELEASE-VALIDATOR. Today it prints nothing; the settings files it covers are ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.claude/settings.local.json and [образец]/.claude/settings.local.json.
Fact (8) cites settings «Where Claude Code keeps the local file in a git repository»: a session started in sai/ keeps its local file at the repo root, <общая папка>/.claude/settings.local.json (git -C sai rev-parse --show-toplevel), and a legacy file in the start directory is still read. «Где что лежит» explains why AC12 covers every settings file.
New design questions: which settings files a session started in sai/ reads, and what CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is for such a session.
AC1(в) runs the real session from <папка Sai> with `pwd` attached, which proves the hook fires from a session started in sai/.

Removed the false sentence «так что дописать событие задним числом нельзя». The text now says the ±60 s check guards only the write route; only the mandate (R2) stops a direct append to the journal file, and the page marks such lines.
AC4 gets a read-side rule. A line is «не из хуков» if (а) its source is not REAL, (б) its time is more than 60 s later than the clock at read time, or (в) its time is more than 120 s earlier than the latest time among earlier lines that are not marked. Such lines are shown with the mark and never used for tasks, states or the office.
120 s is twice the write tolerance, so no line the server accepted can trip rule (в): A.at ≤ t_A+60 and B.at ≥ t_B−60 ≥ t_A−60. Rule (б) stops one hand-written future line from marking every real line after it.
Test in pixel-office-page.test.js: hand-appended SIMULATION, back-dated REAL (−10 min) and future (+1 h) lines, then a real line. The three are marked and excluded; the real one counts.

AC3’s allowlist now includes the linking identifiers tool_response.agentId and tool_input.subagent_type. The rest of tool_response stays forbidden, and session_title is added to the forbidden fields. The marker test puts markers only in forbidden fields and checks that agentId and subagent_type are kept.
New rule AC6 (з): a description is shown only when agent_id, tool_use_id or tool_response.agentId tie it unambiguously to the run; otherwise there is no description, never a guessed one.
Test: two Agent calls of the same subagent_type with different descriptions, then two starts. With the linking events, each task gets its own description and never the other’s; without them, neither task has one.
«Что хранится» gives the reason: SubagentStart and SubagentStop carry only agent_id and agent_type, and WF-06 runs three IDEA-ANALYST runs in parallel. Whether agentId equals agent_id stays a design question.

AC10 is rewritten and states that the handler is a command.
The handler command taken from sai/.claude/settings.json must record the event from any cwd (sai/, sai/tools, a temp folder outside sai/). It must also record it when PATH has no node, or a node other than v22 (e.g. v25.2.1), provided Node 22 exists on the machine.
A hook that cannot start is covered: no hook files where CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR points, or Node 22 not found. In every failure case: exit 0, empty stdout, within 2 s.
Timeout is bounded to 3-5 s with jq `(.timeout // 0) as $t | $t >= 3 and $t <= 5`; dry run: 3 and 5 true, 2, 6 and missing false.
Facts (5) and (7) cite the docs: a hook that can’t start (exit 127) and a timed-out UserPromptSubmit hook both leave notices; handlers run in the current directory; cwd follows `cd`; ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} is «the project root where the session started».

AC2 and AC9 now say `…; echo $?`: no matched lines and exit 1; exit 2 (folder missing) fails. REQ-007 AC6 uses the same form.
Dry runs: plain grep -r on a missing folder gives 2 in both BSD grep and ugrep. BSD grep with --include gives 1 on a missing folder, so no check uses --include.
AC4: tools/test/pixel-office-page.test.js checks the header label «REAL — события хуков Claude Code».
Defined «идущая сессия»: a session_id with an event after the last server start and no session-end event. REQ-007 AC1 uses it for the session count, and its test counts running sessions.

AC6(г): an end-of-turn event with no open row changes nothing, so a start is never invented. Fact (4) cites that after Stop a session may wait for background work to wake it. New design question: does UserPromptSubmit fire when background work wakes the session?

«Сбои (Q10)» now states the remaining case: the end event is lost, the server keeps running, and the session keeps running or is killed without a session-end event. The task then stays «в работе» until the next server start.
AC6(в): next to «в работе» the page shows the task start time and the time of its session’s last event.
AC13: the README gets a subsection «### Ограничения» covering this case, checked by grep -F for «### Ограничения» and «остаться «в работе»».

The handler is stated to be a command. Reasons: AC10 needs exit 0 and empty stdout; AC11 reads the secret from a file; SessionStart accepts only command and mcp_tool; an http handler gets a header secret only from environment variables (allowedEnvVars). Fact (6) cites these.
The command-or-http question is dropped from the design questions; the async question stays. AC10 starts with «обработчик — command».

AC8: if the journal cannot be written (read-only file, full disk), the server answers 500 and keeps serving GET. Tested in tools/test/pixel-office-server.test.js with a read-only journal in a temp folder.

The validator’s note on reading without login is now in the requirement. «Где что лежит» says any account on this computer can read the journal through 127.0.0.1. AC13 requires the README «### Ограничения» to say so, checked by grep -F for «учётная запись».

AC1(в) and (ж) now name the output format: `-p --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-hook-events` (cli-reference). Every hook_response from a Pixel Office handler must have outcome success, exit_code 0 and empty stdout (fields from agent-sdk/typescript SDKHookResponseMessage, fact 11). How to tell those messages apart is a design question.

AC14 pins devDependencies (`jq -c .devDependencies tools/package.json | shasum -a 256` = 54dfc881f13a8b73eeee76ba7bbe3d5e2d15be08dd51ffe2e9e2c9f1464da8fd) and tools/package-lock.json (92d27c4ea99a9e6bb95a4b86bb045a02b934e280e9fe99d8c5c7ab5ed87b5bde). decisions/0002 fixes the dev dependencies (prettier, eslint, @eslint/js, globals), so adding one, for example a DOM library for page tests, needs a decision.
